practices.practice: Read the MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (do not commit credentials) and supply a .env.example with placeholders instead of real secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Never log or store the cluster connection string, LLM API keys, or other secrets; keep a .env.example with placeholders and use a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault or environment variables) for runtime secrets.

practices.practice: Create a single (singleton) MongoClient/Mongoose connection for the process and tune pool and timeout settings for the deployment type (e.g., long-running OLTP: maxPoolSize ~50+, serverSelectionTimeoutMS ~5s; serverless: small maxPoolSize 3–5 and low maxIdleTimeMS).
practices.prior_belief: Read the MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and configure Mongoose to use the unified topology, a bounded connection pool (e.g. maxPoolSize: 50), and a serverSelectionTimeoutMS to fail fast; never embed credentials in code or config files.

practices.practice: Enforce TLS for all client connections and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for all connections (use tls=true / ssl=true in the connection string or Mongoose tls options) and validate the server certificate (set rejectUnauthorized: true or provide CA file) so credentials and vectors are sent encrypted.

practices.practice: Use Private Endpoint (Private Link) and cluster firewall rules to restrict network access; disable public access in production where possible.
practices.source_name: Enable private access in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC and per-application, least-privilege database accounts rather than long-lived master keys.
practices.prior_belief: Use a least-privilege database account for the app (create a Mongo user with only the required roles/privileges for the sample database) and rotate credentials regularly rather than using a master key.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (azure-terraform)

practices.practice: Use customer-managed keys (Key Vault CMK) for data-at-rest encryption on regulated workloads and plan key lifecycle/rotation via Azure Key Vault.
practices.source_name: Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

practices.practice: Pick a shard (partition) key so related versions are colocated (e.g., choose the field most commonly used in equality filters such as assetId so all versions for one asset reside in the same partition), and shard only when a single-shard's capacity is insufficient.
practices.prior_belief: Partition documents so that all versions of an asset share the same partition key (use assetId as partition key) to keep versioned documents colocated and avoid cross-partition aggregation costs.

practices.practice: Create a compound index that follows ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) so latest-version lookups use assetId (equality) then version (sort) to avoid blocking sorts and COLLSCANs.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index on { assetId: 1, version: -1, createdAt: -1 } to efficiently query the latest version(s) per asset and support range queries over versions by createdAt.

practices.practice: Use sparse or partial indexes for optional LLM-derived fields (e.g., llmTags.eligibilityTier) to reduce index size and RU costs rather than indexing them unconditionally.
practices.prior_belief: Limit indexed fields and use sparse/partial indexes for optional LLM-derived fields (e.g., eligibilityTier) to reduce index size and RU costs; avoid indexing large text or vector fields with general-purpose indexes.

practices.practice: Do not index high-dimensional vectors with standard B-tree indexes; use the platform's vector index (cosmosSearch) and keep vector dimensions and dtype consistent across documents.
practices.prior_belief: If using vectors, avoid indexing the raw high-dimensional vector field with standard B-tree indexes; instead rely on the platform's vector-index feature (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and keep vector dimension and dtype consistent across documents.

practices.practice: Choose the appropriate cosmosSearch index type by scale (vector-ivf under ~10k, vector-hnsw up to ~50k, vector-diskann for 100k+/production) and tune parameters (dimensions, similarity, lBuild / lSearch / maxDegree).
Create vector indexes with explicit cosmosSearch options (dimensions, similarity, kind) using the service's index creation command rather than relying on naive schema mappings.
practices.prior_belief: Do vector indexing configuration out-of-band (via the cluster/index tools) specifying algorithm (HNSW/IVF), M or efConstruction for HNSW, and ensure the index's dimension matches stored vectors; do not attempt to create such indexes via naive schema mappings.

practices.practice: Use the service's $search / createSearchIndexes for full-text search (BM25) and prefer that over community `$text` when building search experiences.

Run server-side aggregation pipelines (db.collection.aggregate) for summaries and push selective $match/$project stages early (ideally scoped to the partition key) to reduce work and avoid cross-partition scans.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side aggregation pipelines (db.collection.aggregate) for computing totals and coverage ratios instead of loading all documents into the application; craft the pipeline to filter by partition key to avoid cross-partition scans.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') to verify index usage and to compare keysExamined/docsExamined to nReturned when optimizing aggregation or queries.
Implement retries with exponential backoff for throttling (429 / RequestRateTooLarge) and honor service retry headers (Retry-After or x-ms-retry-after-ms) when present.
practices.prior_belief: Handle 429/RequestRateTooLarge by implementing retries with exponential backoff and honoring any Retry-After or x-ms-retry-after-ms response header values returned by the service.

practices.practice: Monitor cluster RU/CPU/IOPS/storage/connection metrics and enable diagnostic slow-query logs (Log Analytics) and alerts tailored to your chosen tier to detect saturation early.
Make seed scripts idempotent by using upsert keyed on a natural unique key (e.g., assetId + version) or by checking existence before insert, and enforce uniqueness with a unique index.
practices.how_found: update examples; search 'upsert example Azure DocumentDB'

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes to automatically expire history documents but ensure the TTL field is a Date, be aware deletions are backgrounded (~60s granularity), and do not rely on TTL for critical audit retention without policy review.
practices.prior_belief: Create TTL indexes if you need to automatically expire old history documents (e.g., ttlSeconds on createdAt) but only after verifying RU impact and retention policies; do not rely on TTL for critical audit history unless policy allows.

practices.practice: Keep the per-collection index budget modest (review unused indexes with $indexStats) and avoid indexing large text or vector fields with general-purpose B-tree indexes.
Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity, store the embedding model name and dimensions alongside vectors, and consider product quantization or fp16 to trade memory for minor recall loss.
Tune connection pool sizes and concurrent query counts to the cluster's connection limits and RU budget, and close the Mongoose connection gracefully on process exit.
practices.prior_belief: Keep connection pool sizes and concurrent query counts tuned to the RU budget and the cluster's connection limits; close the Mongoose connection gracefully on process exit to avoid leaking connections.

practices.practice: When building coverage or aggregate pipelines, push filters and projections early (match → project → group) and scope by partition key to reduce scanned documents and allow indexes to help.
practices.prior_belief: When aggregating coverage ratio, design the pipeline to push filters and projections early (use $match on partition key/asset type, then $group) so the work is reduced and indexes can be used; use $project to include only numeric fields used in sums.

practices.practice: Protect LLM API keys and secrets by calling LLMs from a backend service, storing keys in Key Vault, and avoiding persisting raw API keys or prompts in application logs or the database.
practices.prior_belief: Protect LLM classification step and its API key: call the LLM from a backend service (not client-side), cache classification results on the document, and never persist raw LLM prompts or API keys in the database.

practices.practice: Prefer the service's managed index lifecycle workflow (hide → verify → drop) when reducing indexes; verify index use with explain before dropping indexes.

When obtaining the connection string for an app, use the portal or role-based methods and prefer the mongodb+srv form with tls=true and recommended driver options (e.g., retryWrites=false, maxIdleTimeMS).

practices.practice: Choose read preference for your distribution: use nearest for latency, primaryPreferred (or primary) for read-after-write consistency in a single primary region, and tag-aware preferences for region-specific reads.

practices.practice: Avoid enabling retryWrites in connection strings for this managed service where the docs show it as false in examples (use the provider/portal-retrieved string as authoritative).
practices.source_name: Deploy Azure DocumentDB (Bicep / CLI) — connection string guidance

practices.practice: Use Key Vault to store runtime secrets (DB connection strings, OpenAI keys) and reference them (managed identity / Key Vault references) rather than embedding secrets in parameters or code.
practices.source_name: Apps, API Keys, and Azure Key Vault secrets

practices.practice: Write unit tests that mock the database and LLM services, and run a small, idempotent integration/seed step only behind an environment flag for live-cluster verification.
practices.prior_belief: Use testing practices that mock the DB and LLM for unit tests (so tests run offline) and include a small integration/seeding step keyed behind an environment flag for live-cluster verification only.
practices.source_name: How to build confidence in Azure workloads with effective testing / Unit testing best practices

practices.practice: Do not assume platform behavior from other MongoDB-compatible services; use the Azure DocumentDB compatibility docs (unsupported operators and behavior) and run a compatibility assessment before migration.

practices.practice: When seeding or migrating data, verify and sync indexes (e.g., Collateral.syncIndexes()) so schema/index creation completes before heavy writes or queries.
For production vector workloads on M30+, prefer DiskANN indexes for scale and tune lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree and consider product quantization or fp16 to reduce memory.

notes:
I inspected the app (models, routes, seed script, and LLM classifier) and used Microsoft Learn docs and the installed DocumentDB skills to gather public guidance that maps directly to the app's areas: connection handling, security/auth, partitioning/sharding, indexing, vector search, aggregation/queries, monitoring/retries, seeding, TTL and testing. Most of the prior beliefs (K01–K09, K11–K09, K12–K22) were supported by Azure DocumentDB docs or the installed DocumentDB skills; the exception is K10 (prefer optimistic concurrency over multi-document transactions): I found no Azure DocumentDB public guidance that explicitly recommends preferring an application-level version field over transactions for versioned documents (I searched with the queries above), so K10 is recorded as prior_knowledge_only.
